# Incoming Damage / Max Hit / EHP

- **Status:** ⚠️ Unverified
- **Mechanic tags:** defense, ehp, max-hit, mitigation

## Setup

Config → Enemy: pick an enemy + skill (Test Enemy → Test Attack / Test Spell, prefilled 1000 per hit type — editable). The Player Stats screen shows an 'Effective HP / Max Hit' panel under the offense result with per-type Incoming → Mitigated → Max Hit → EHP.

## Raw data points

Per-formula math is Help-DB sourced (armour, resistance, block, evasion, avoidance — see their own entries). The MITIGATION ORDER and the composition of the incoming chain are NOT yet confirmed in-game. Real enemy incoming-damage magnitudes are not in any dataset — the 1000/type values are placeholders the owner replaces with measured hits.

## Derived / confirmed formula

Per type T: always-on taken fraction f_T = (1 − armour_mit if hit) × (1 − resist_T) × (1 + Σ damage-taken-additional). Max Hit = pool ÷ f_T (pool = unsealed Life + ES + Barrier while active; worst case — no evade/avoid/block). EHP = pool ÷ [f_T × (1 − evade) × (1 − avoid) × (1 − block_chance × block_ratio)]. DoT rows skip armour + block + evade (resistance + DoT damage-taken only). Evasion/Block pick the attack- or spell-side value from the enemy skill's kind. Chance to Avoid Damage is a single value (defense.dmg_avoid_chance) applied uniformly to every type — in-game it rolls independently per type, but the per-type EHP figure is unaffected by that independence, so a single value is exact for this metric.

## Notes / caveats / open questions

OPEN / needs-verification: (1) the mitigation order of operations; (2) how the Barrier pool absorbs a hit (currently added to the survivable pool — the absorption-rate application is not modeled per-hit); (3) damage-taken-AS conversions (physical_taken_as_fire etc.) are parsed but NOT yet applied — a labeled follow-up; (4) conditional damage-taken scoping (e.g. 'during restoration effect') is applied via the normal condition gate, not per-line. Enemy incoming magnitudes are owner-measured (deferred behind the 1000 placeholder).

## Implementation (engine model)

engine/defense.py::calculate_incoming (+ _incoming_taken_fraction, _dmg_taken_factor); wired in compute.py, returned as StatResult.incoming (server.py 'incoming'). The damage-taken family (dmg_taken_additional + physical/elemental/hit/dot) is now CONSUMED here — Tenacity and other damage-taken sources finally apply. Enemy skill config: renderer utils/enemyPresets.ts (static registry) + per-loadout EnemyIncomingConfig (buildStore) → server EnemyIncomingRequest → BuildInput/BuildSource.enemy_config. UI: PlayerStatsScreen.tsx IncomingPanel (left column, under offense); editor in BuildOverviewScreen.tsx (Config → Enemy).
